bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

# git-trim

git-trim automatically trims local tracking branches whose upstream branches are merged or removed.

Installation

- Download a prebuilt binary from the Releases page and place it in a directory on your PATH.

Usage

- Run `git trim` in a repository to detect and optionally delete local branches that are merged or whose upstreams are gone.
- Use `git trim --dry-run` to see what would be deleted without making changes.
- For full command-line options and detailed usage, see the included man page: `docs/git-trim.man`.

Screenshots and Examples

- A screencast and example images may be available in the repository (e.g. `screencast.png`, `images/`).

GIT-TRIM(1)                                    General Commands Manual                                    GIT-TRIM(1)

NAME
       git-trim - Automatically trims your tracking branches whose upstream branches are merged or stray.

SYNOPSIS
       git-trim [FLAGS] [OPTIONS]

FLAGS
       -h, --help
              Prints help information

       --no-update
              Do not update remotes [config: trim.update]

       --no-confirm
              Do not ask confirm [config: trim.confirm]

       --no-detach
              Do not detach when HEAD is about to be deleted [config: trim.detach]

       --dry-run
              Do not delete branches, show what branches will be deleted

OPTIONS
       -b, --bases=bases
              Comma separated multiple names of branches. All the other branches are compared with the upstream
              branches of those branches. [default: branches that tracks `git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/*/HEAD`]
              [config: trim.bases]

              The default value is a branch that tracks `git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/*/HEAD`. They might not be
              reflected correctly when the HEAD branch of your remote repository is changed. You can see the changed
              HEAD branch name with `git remote show <remote>` and apply it to your local repository with `git remote
              set-head <remote> --auto`.

       -p, --protected=protected
              Comma separated multiple glob patterns (e.g. `release-*`, `feature/*`) of branches that should never be
              deleted. [config: trim.protected]

       --update-interval=update_interval
              Prevents too frequent updates. Seconds between updates in seconds. 0 to disable. [default: 5] [config:
              trim.updateInterval]

       -d, --delete=delete
              Comma separated values of `<delete range>[:<remote name>]`. Delete range is one of the `merged,
              merged-local, merged-remote, stray, diverged, local, remote`. `:<remote name>` is only necessary to a
              `<delete range>` when the range is applied to remote branches. You can use `*` as `<remote name>` to
              delete a range of branches from all remotes. [default : `merged:origin`] [config: trim.delete]

              `merged` implies `merged-local,merged-remote`.

              `merged-local` will delete merged tracking local branches. `merged-remote:<remote>` will delete merged
              upstream branches from `<remote>`. `stray` will delete tracking local branches, which is not merged,

import pty, os, subprocess, sys, select, time

def run_with_pty(stdin_is_tty, stderr_is_tty, stdout_is_tty, input_data="y\n"):
    # We'll use subprocess with different redirections
    # For tty, we need a pty pair
    # Simplify: test current behavior by checking isatty in child?
    pass

# Case A: stdin pipe, stderr tty, stdout tty -> need to run executable directly with stdin from pipe but stderr/stdout to pty
# We can do: script -qec "executable --no-update < /tmp/input.txt" 
# where /tmp/input.txt contains "y\n" but child's stdin is still pty? Actually "<" redirects child's stdin to file, not pty.
# So we can test stdin=file, stderr/stdout=pty

import subprocess, textwrap
def test(cmd, input_file=None):
    print(f"CMD: {cmd} input_file={input_file}")
    # Use script to provide tty for stdout/stderr, but redirect stdin if requested
    full = cmd
    result = subprocess.run(["script","-qec", full, "/dev/null"], input=input_file, capture_output=True, text=True)
    print("returncode:", result.returncode)
    print("stdout:", repr(result.stdout[:2000]))
    print("stderr:", repr(result.stderr[:2000]))
    print("----")

# Need a deletable branch first

function.arguments:
{"command": "cd /tmp && rm -rf origin3 work3 && mkdir origin3 && (cd origin3 && git init -q --bare . && git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/main) && git clone -q origin3 work3 2>&1; cd work3 && git config user.email "t@t.com" && git config user.name "t" && git commit -q --allow-empty -m init && git push -q -u origin HEAD:main 2>&1; git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD refs/remotes/origin/main
echo "base ready"; git branch -vv; git branch -a
# Create:
# 1. merged tracking (featMerged) - merged into main
git checkout -qb featMerged; echo m > m.txt; git add m.txt; git commit -qm "m"; git push -qu origin featMerged 2>&1 >/dev/null; git checkout -q main; git merge -q --no-ff featMerged -m "merge"; git push -q origin main 2>&1
echo "featMerged done"
# 2. stray: tracking with upstream gone, not merged
git checkout -qb featStray; echo s > s.txt; git add s.txt; git commit -qm "s"; git push -qu origin featStray 2>&1 >/dev/null; git push -q origin --delete featStray 2>&1; git fetch -q -p origin 2>&1
echo "featStray done (upstream deleted)"; git branch -vv; git status 2>&1 | head
# 3. local non-tracking merged (localMerged)
git checkout -qb localMerged; echo l > l.txt; git add l.txt; git commit -qm "l"; git checkout -q main; git merge -q --no-ff localMerged -m "merge local"; git push -q origin main 2>&1
echo "localMerged done (no upstream)"; git branch -vv
# 4. remote non-upstream merged (remoteMerged): push branch then delete local, keep remote merged?
git checkout -qb tmpRemote; echo r > r.txt; git add r.txt; git commit -qm "r"; git push -q origin tmpRemote:remoteMerged 2>&1; git checkout -q main; git merge -q --no-ff tmpRemote -m "merge remote" 2>&1 || { git merge -q --no-ff origin/remoteMerged -m "merge remote" 2>&1; }; git push -q origin main 2>&1; git branch -D tmpRemote 2>&1
echo "remoteMerged done"; git branch -a; git log --oneline --all --graph | head -20
# 5. diverged: tracking where local and remote diverged, local merged? Need to understand diverged definition: man says diverged will delete merged tracking local and upstreams even if upstreams are not merged and diverged. Hmm.
# Let's create diverged: push, then local extra commit merged into main, remote extra different commit not merged?
git checkout -qb featDiverged; echo d1 > d.txt; git add d.txt; git commit -qm "d1"; git push -qu origin featDiverged 2>&1 >/dev/null; echo d2 >> d.txt; git commit -qam "d2 local"; git push -q origin featDiverged 2>&1 || true
# Actually to diverge, need remote to have different commit: push, then amend remote via another clone? Simpler: create branch, push, then local commit, then force-push remote with different commit?
# Let's just create a branch where local and upstream point to different commits, both not merged? Need to experiment.
git branch -vv; git branch -a
"}

# git-trim

git-trim automatically trims local tracking branches whose upstream branches are merged or removed.

Installation

- Download a prebuilt binary from the Releases page and place it in a directory on your PATH.

Usage

- Run `git trim` in a repository to detect and optionally delete local branches that are merged or whose upstreams are gone.
- Use `git trim --dry-run` to see what would be deleted without making changes.
- For full command-line options and detailed usage, see the included man page: `docs/git-trim.man`.

Screenshots and Examples

fn get_remote_branches(repo: &git2::Repository) -> Vec<(String, String, git2::Oid)> {
    let mut res = Vec::new();
    if let Ok(iter) = repo.branches(Some(git2::BranchType::Remote)) {
        for b in iter {
            if let Ok((br, _)) = b {
                if let Ok(name) = br.name() {
                    if let Some(n) = name {
                        // Exclude symbolic refs like origin/HEAD? br.get().is_symbolic()? Check via reference?
                        // Use br.get() reference
                        let refr = br.get();
                        if refr.kind() == Some(git2::ReferenceType::Symbolic) {
                            continue;
                        }
                        // Also exclude if name ends with /HEAD? e.g., origin/HEAD
                        if n.ends_with("/HEAD") {
                            continue;
                        }
                        let full = refr.name().unwrap_or("").to_string();
                        let oid = refr.resolve().ok().and_then(|r| r.target()).or_else(|| refr.target()).unwrap_or(git2::Oid::from_str("0000000000000000000000000000000000000000").unwrap());
                        res.push((n.to_string(), full, oid));
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    res
}

fn is_ancestor(repo: &git2::Repository, ancestor: git2::Oid, descendant: git2::Oid) -> bool {
    if ancestor == descendant {
        return true;
    }
    match repo.graph_descendant_of(descendant, ancestor) {
        Ok(v) => v,
        Err(_) => false,
    }
}
